basis: Oral and limb defects define OFD4; intellectual disability and airway malformations each 80-99%; hearing loss (80-99%) and eye movement abnormalities omitted by cap.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: choanal atresia and laryngomalacia are structural airway defects, each annotated 80-99%; severe airway compromise takes priority at the cap.
decisions.otologic: none: conductive hearing impairment qualifies at 80-99%, but is omitted under the four-axis cap in favor of defining oral/limb defects, neurologic impairment and airway compromise.

basis: Umbrella glycosylation defect; subtype-specific skin and neurologic findings cannot establish group-wide frequencies. [Orphanet](https://www.orpha.net/en/disease/detail/309778)

decisions.neurologic: none: neurodevelopmental impairment occurs in particular subtypes; frequency >=30% across this heterogeneous glycosylation group is unestablished.
decisions.dermatologic: none: cutis laxa characterizes specific subtypes, but the evidence does not establish it as defining or present in >=30% across the whole group.

basis: Strabismus 55%; skeletal anomalies 83%; renal malformations 38%; cardiac defects 33% omitted by cap. [Cohort](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34521999/)

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: structural joint/limb abnormalities occur in 40/48 (83%); joint hypermobility is also annotated 30-79%; this extends beyond central hypotonia.

basis: Primary microcephaly with cortical maldevelopment and intellectual disability; hearing loss in one annotated patient cannot establish >=30% involvement across the disease.

decisions.otologic: none: mixed hearing impairment in 1/1 selectively annotated patient is insufficient to establish a >=30% disease-wide frequency; it is not a defining criterion.

basis: Folate deficiency impairs marrow DNA synthesis and causes megaloblastic anemia; nutritional deficiency alone does not establish an additional metabolic/endocrine disorder.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: this concept defines a nutritional anemia, without an independent endocrine, electrolyte or inborn metabolic disorder; altered cellular metabolism alone is insufficient.

basis: Open lumbosacral cord and vertebral defect; persistent bladder dysfunction (~70-90%) and bowel dysfunction (>50%) result directly from sacral denervation.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: direct sacral denervation causes persistent loss of bowel evacuation/continence in most patients (>50%); this is intrinsic functional impairment, not merely constipation risk.

basis: Inborn organic-acid metabolic defect with defining developmental delay and CNS abnormalities; retinal mottling alone does not prove dysfunction, and cataract frequency is unknown.

decisions.neurologic: primary: developmental delay defines the recognized clinical phenotype, supported by structural CNS abnormalities. [Orphanet](https://www.orpha.net/en/disease/detail/289307)

basis: Aortic and skeletal pathology define disease; ectopia lentis is a major diagnostic criterion. Pneumothorax is uncommon; striae and dural ectasia alone do not establish functional damage.

decisions.pulmonary: none: pneumothorax occurred in 11/249 (4.4%); the supplied 80-99% annotation conflicts with clinical data. [Cohort](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/6732339/)

basis: Intellectual disability and defining eyelid defects (ptosis 90%); cardiac defects and hearing loss each 30-79%; polydactyly (47%) and cleft palate omitted by cap.

decisions.ocular: primary: ptosis and blepharophimosis are defining eyelid malformations in the definition and parent syndrome; ptosis is documented in 18/20 (90%).

basis: Inherited mitochondrial iron-sulfur/heme metabolic defect causes defining anemia and cerebellar disease; ocular motor signs reflect neurologic dysfunction.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: inherited mitochondrial iron-sulfur/heme metabolism defect warrants the metabolic mechanism axis. [Orphanet](https://www.orpha.net/en/disease/detail/2802)
